newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown says monetary process could be improved.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown says monetary process could be improved.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, said the existing procedure for setting monetary policy was not as good as it could be and should be reformed.
In an interview with the Evening Standard newspaper, he appeared to suggest that the results of monetary meetings should be made known immediately.

"If the meetings were regularly timed, if the publication of results was instantaneous, if a number of other changes were made, there would be more certainty and rationality about the process," Brown said.

At present, the Bank of England announces any change in official interest rates during the next round of money market operations, which may be the day after a meeting, but it makes no formal announcement if rates are unchanged.
Brown said that as Chancellor of the Exchequer, he would continue with the system of monthly monetary meetings, but the present system should be made "more objective, less personalised."
"We have now got these unseemly rows between the Governor and the Chancellor," he said in a reference to the present disagreement between the two officials over interest rates.
The Bank's track record should be examined and it should be able to draw upon a broader range of expertise, "including independent people," in making its recommendations.
